_meta.note: The bundled cascade_cms/*.py files are ground truth. This schema is a fast-lookup summary; read the source when it is not detailed enough.

key_behaviors.entry_point: CascadeWrapperBase(environment_variables, configuration_variables, debug=None) used as a context manager. Never import cascade_cms.driver, never manage an asyncio loop, never construct an aiohttp ClientSession.
key_behaviors.queue_then_submit: Operations methods QUEUE a request; nothing hits the network until cascade.submit_requests(). submit_requests() clears the queue, so each batch is independent.
key_behaviors.completion_order: submit_requests() returns results in COMPLETION order, not submission order. Never zip results back to the request list by position — identify each result from its own contents.
key_behaviors.errors_are_values: A failed operation returns a CascadeError instead of its success type; it does not raise. Requests that error at the Python level are logged and DROPPED from the returned list, so len(results) can be < number queued.
key_behaviors.write_ops_return_success: Every write operation returns CascadeSuccess ({"success": true}) via parser=parse_success — NOT CascadeError, which is only the failure branch. checkOut is the exception: it returns CheckedOutAsset.
key_behaviors.callbacks: .then(fn) or .then([fn, ...]) registers callbacks run per-result after the batch. Sequential per result, concurrent across results. Async callbacks are awaited; sync callbacks run in an Executor (ThreadPoolExecutor default, pass ProcessPoolExecutor for CPU-bound work via submit_requests(executor=...)). A callback that raises is logged and swallowed — the batch continues.
key_behaviors.caching: Only GET responses are cached (SQLiteBackend), and only successful parses are cacheable.
key_behaviors.hex_uuid_serialization: Cascade rejects dashed UUIDs. IdentifierType.identifier, NewAsset.site_id and NewAsset.parent_folder_id all serialize as bare hex (uuid.UUID.hex) via field serializers. Pass real uuid.UUID objects; the library handles the format.

IdentifierType.purpose: Reference an asset by UUID. Frozen, extra="forbid", populate_by_name=True.

fields.id: uuid.UUID — required. Field name is `identifier`, alias `id`. Serialized as bare hex.
fields.type: AssetTypes — required. Field name is `asset_type`, alias `type`.

IdentifierType.rejects: A model_validator raises ValueError('Identifier payload contains unexpected fields: [...]') for ANY other key. `asset_type`/`identifier` are accepted as aliases and rewritten to `type`/`id`.

properties.get_path: path string, or None when `path` is unset
properties.get_sitename: site name, or None when `path` is unset
properties.get_site_id: site UUID, or None when `path` is unset

Path.purpose: Reference an asset by site + site-relative path. A plain TypedDict (a dict literal), NOT a Pydantic model — nothing validates it at construction.

keys.asset_type: AssetTypes — required to build the URL
keys.siteName: str — declared Optional on the TypedDict but REQUIRED in practice

Path.gotcha: resolve_identifier() raises ValueError('Path identifiers require siteName to build the request URL') when siteName is None or absent. This is a runtime check, not a schema check.

identifiers.resolve_identifier: IdentifierType -> (asset_type, hex_id); Path -> (asset_type, siteName, path). These become the URL segments after the operation name.

read.returns: Asset on success, CascadeError on failure
read.notes: Accepts a single identifier or a list; each becomes its own queued request.

create.returns: IdentifierType (the new asset's id + type) on success, CascadeError on failure
create.notes: The response only carries createdAssetId, so the parser re-injects asset_type from the payload via functools.partial.

edit.returns: CascadeSuccess on success, CascadeError on failure
edit.notes: Takes the Asset objects returned by read(), after mutation.

delete.signature: delete(identifier: IdentifierType | Path, payload: deleteParameters | None = None, parser=parse_success)
delete.returns: CascadeSuccess on success, CascadeError on failure

copy.signature: copy(identifier: IdentifierType | Path | list[...], payload: copyParameters, parser=parse_success)
copy.returns: CascadeSuccess on success, CascadeError on failure

move.signature: move(identifier: IdentifierType | Path | list[...], payload: moveParameters, parser=parse_success)
move.returns: CascadeSuccess on success, CascadeError on failure

publish.signature: publish(identifier: IdentifierType | Path | list[...], payload: publishInformation | None = None, parser=parse_success)
publish.returns: CascadeSuccess on success, CascadeError on failure

search.returns: ListElements on success, CascadeError on failure
search.notes: Asserts the payload is a SearchInformation instance.

checkIn.signature: checkIn(identifier: IdentifierType | Path | list[...], payload: Comment, parser=parse_success)
checkIn.returns: CascadeSuccess on success, CascadeError on failure
checkIn.notes: Toggles an in-process checkout ledger that is NOT synced with the server's real lock state.

checkOut.returns: CheckedOutAsset (has .workingCopyIdentifier) on success, CascadeError on failure
checkOut.notes: The one write-shaped operation that does NOT return CascadeSuccess.

siteCopy.returns: CascadeSuccess on success, CascadeError on failure

listSites.returns: ListElements on success, CascadeError on failure

listSubscribers.returns: ListElements on success, CascadeError on failure
listSubscribers.notes: Returns None, not Self — cannot be chained with .then().

readAudits.returns: ListElements on success, CascadeError on failure

readAccessRights.returns: accessRightsInformationPayload on success, CascadeError on failure

editAccessRights.returns: CascadeSuccess on success, CascadeError on failure

readWorkflowSettings.returns: workflowSettingsPayload on success, CascadeError on failure

editWorkflowSettings.returns: CascadeSuccess on success, CascadeError on failure
editWorkflowSettings.notes: Returns None, not Self. Builds its URL from payload.body['identifier'].

readWorkflowInformation.returns: workflowInformation on success, CascadeError on failure

performWorkflowTransition.signature: performWorkflowTransition(identifier: IdentifierType | Path, payload: workflowTransitionInformation, parser=parse_success)
performWorkflowTransition.returns: CascadeSuccess on success, CascadeError on failure

listMessages.returns: ListElements on success, CascadeError on failure

markMessage.returns: CascadeSuccess on success, CascadeError on failure

deleteMessage.returns: CascadeSuccess on success, CascadeError on failure

readPreferences.returns: SimplePayload on success, CascadeError on failure

editPreference.returns: CascadeSuccess on success, CascadeError on failure

payload_models._note: All inherit SimplePayload, whose @model_serializer format_builder wraps the body as {"<lowercasedClassName>": {...aliased fields...}}. Construct with the PYTHON field name or its alias (populate_by_name=True); the alias is what goes on the wire.

alternatives: exactly one of site_name (alias siteName) or site_id (alias siteId)
exactly one of parent_folder_path (alias parentFolderPath) or parent_folder_id (alias parentFolderId)
NewAsset.extra: allow — asset-type-specific fields (title, xhtml, metadata...) pass straight through
NewAsset.serialization: {"asset": {"<asset_type>": {...}}}; site_id/parent_folder_id emit bare hex; None values are dropped
NewAsset.error_if_violated: ValueError('Provide exactly one of site_name or site_id') / ('Provide exactly one of parent_folder_path or parent_folder_id')

fields.new_name: str = "", alias newName — empty means no rename

fields.unpublish: bool = True — set False to publish rather than unpublish

fields.transition_comment: str | None, alias transitionComment — required key

fields.by_identifier: IdentifierType, alias identifier — required, MUST be of type user/role/group

fields.body: AccessRightsModel {user_id(alias identifier): IdentifierType, acl_entries(alias aclEntries): list[Entries], allLevel: none|read|write}, alias accessRightsInformation — required

WorkflowSettingsModel {identifier: IdentifierType, workflowDefinitions: list[IdentifierType], inheritedWorkflowDefinitions: list[IdentifierType], inheritWorkflows: bool, requireWorkflow: bool}, alias workflowSettings — required

response_models.Asset: Dict-backed wrapper, NOT a Pydantic model. Read with .get(key), write with attribute assignment (asset.field = value) — there is no __setitem__/__getitem__. .asset_type property. get_data_structure() / get_page_configuration() return LIVE references. See references/asset_api.md.
response_models.CascadeSuccess: {"success": true}. Frozen. The success return of every write operation.
response_models.CascadeError: {"success": false, "message": str}. Frozen. Returned as a VALUE by any operation that fails.
response_models.IdentifierType: See identifiers above. Returned by create.
response_models.ListElements: Frozen; .elements / .flat -> list[IdentifierType | Message | Audit]. Returned by all list-shaped endpoints.
response_models.workflowInformation: Frozen. .related_entity, .current_step, .ordered_steps, .unordered_steps, .start_date, .end_date, .name, .workflow_info_id. Steps are TypedDicts: {step_identifier, label, step_type, actions, owner}; actions: {action_identifier, label, action_type, next_id}.
response_models.accessRightsInformationPayload: See payload_models — same model is used for read and write.
response_models.workflowSettingsPayload: See payload_models — same model is used for read and write.

parsers._note: Every parser tries CascadeError FIRST and falls back to the success type. That is why failures arrive as values instead of exceptions.

environment_variables.CASCADE_URL: base URL of the instance — required
environment_variables.SERVER: label used in logfile naming — required

environment_and_config.configuration_variables: kwargs forwarded to the SQLiteBackend cache: cache_name, allowed_codes, allowed_methods, expire_after. Pass {} for defaults.
environment_and_config.debug_config: Optional 3rd arg to CascadeWrapperBase. Omit it (default None) for normal logging to ./logs/{SERVER}_{timestamp}.log. Debug mode requires a FULLY specified dict — every key present, no inferred defaults — and writes ./logs/{SERVER}_debug_{timestamp}.log.
